svg.aria-label: How to write 語: 14 strokes · 13 pen lifts · 17 movements
svg.title: Writing 語
svg.desc: 17 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of 語 (japanese), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansJP-Subset.ttf. Stroke order after KanjiVG, kanji/08a9e.svg, kanji 語 (U+8A9E CJK UNIFIED IDEOGRAPH-8A9E), fourteen stroke paths kvg:08a9e-s1 to s14 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0) <https://github.com/KanjiVG/kanjivg/blob/master/kanji/08a9e.svg>. Source note on variation: KanjiVG stores each stroke as one directed path in writing order: s1 to s7 are 言, s8 to s11 五 and s12 to s14 口, each drawn in the same order and directions as KanjiVG's own files for those three, kanji/08a00.svg, 04e94.svg and 053e3.svg. Only the order and direction are taken from that file. The learner path's coordinates are the bundled Noto Sans JP outline's own medial line, so the print glyph's proportions, not KanjiVG's handwriting-style ones, decide where each stroke runs. As in 言, KanjiVG's first path is a dot drawn down to the right (kvg:type ㇔). The Japanese print glyph draws that mark as a short bar, so the path runs along the bar from left to right.
svg.text: How it is written — 14 strokes · 13 pen lifts · 17 movements
Stroke order after KanjiVG, kanji/08a9e.svg, kanji 語 (U+8A9E CJK UNIFIED IDEOGRAPH-8A9E), fourteen stroke paths kvg:08a9e-s1 to s14 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0)
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
